title: How S. Tara Singh Attained Martyrdom

blocks.text: Dohra:

Moman Khan launched on an expedition to crush the Singhs, Accompanied by a host of Muslim warriors. Taking advantage of the darkness of the night ahead, They intended to take on the Singhs unawares. (1)
lines: Moman Khan launched on an expedition to crush the Singhs,
Accompanied by a host of Muslim warriors.
Taking advantage of the darkness of the night ahead,
They intended to take on the Singhs unawares.

blocks.text: Then (a local resident) Ghumanda1 , an Uppal Jat by caste, Went ahead and accosted the advancing troops. Saying that since the Mughal troops were searching for S. Tara Singh, He volunteered to guide the troops to Tara Singh's place. (2)
lines: Then (a local resident) Ghumanda1 , an Uppal Jat by caste,
Went ahead and accosted the advancing troops.
Saying that since the Mughal troops were searching for S.
Tara Singh,
He volunteered to guide the troops to Tara Singh's place.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

So (Ghamanda Jat) leading Moman Khan's troops from the front, Led them on a circuitous route somewhat away from the Singhs' location. He directed the Mughal troops towards village Dalla, Perhaps because he nursed some old grouse against the village. (3)
lines: So (Ghamanda Jat) leading Moman Khan's troops from the front,
Led them on a circuitous route somewhat away from the Singhs' location.
He directed the Mughal troops towards village Dalla,
Perhaps because he nursed some old grouse against the village.

blocks.text: Or he had thought of doing some favour to the Singhs, Because the delay in troops' arrival would enable the Singhs to escape. (Simultaneously), he sent a message to the Singhs, That S. Tara Singh should vacate his place with his companions. (4)
lines: Or he had thought of doing some favour to the Singhs,
Because the delay in troops' arrival would enable the Singhs to escape.
(Simultaneously), he sent a message to the Singhs,
That S.
Tara Singh should vacate his place with his companions.

blocks.text: That way when the Mughal troops returned to Lahore empty handed, S. Tara Singh should return to occupy his place. Since a moment's escape could ensure his survival for years, Why should he lose his precious life in vain. (5)
lines: That way when the Mughal troops returned to Lahore empty handed,
S.
Tara Singh should return to occupy his place.
Since a moment's escape could ensure his survival for years,
Why should he lose his precious life in vain.

blocks.text: Hearing this message, S. Tara Singh addressed the messenger, That he (Tara Singh) acknowledged the messenger's well-meaning intentions, That the latter had indeed done a noble deed (by informing him), For the sake of maintaining his fraternal bonds. (6)
lines: Hearing this message,
S.
Tara Singh addressed the messenger,
That he (Tara Singh) acknowledged the messenger's well-meaning intentions,
That the latter had indeed done a noble deed (by informing him),
For the sake of maintaining his fraternal bonds.

blocks.text: Dohra:

No doubt, what he had conveyed was for the former's benefit, And it was also factually correct (to adopt this strategy). But since he (Tara Singh) had resolved to make a sacrifice, He would not run away anywhere from there. (7)
lines: No doubt, what he had conveyed was for the former's benefit,
And it was also factually correct (to adopt this strategy).
But since he (Tara Singh) had resolved to make a sacrifice,
He would not run away anywhere from there.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

He could very well run away to save his life, And could easily return to his place as well. But since his fraternity would accuse him of being a coward, So he would never run away to save his life. (8)
lines: He could very well run away to save his life,
And could easily return to his place as well.
But since his fraternity would accuse him of being a coward,
So he would never run away to save his life.

blocks.text: On the other hand, hearing about the arrival of troops, The residents of Dalla village came out to meet them. Assuring that they being the loyal subjects of the Mughal sovereign, Their entire village had no rebel Singh among them. (9)
lines: On the other hand, hearing about the arrival of troops,
The residents of Dalla village came out to meet them.
Assuring that they being the loyal subjects of the Mughal sovereign,
Their entire village had no rebel Singh among them.

blocks.text: The Singhs then challenged the Mughals with the beat of a drum, Which the Mughal troops heard from a distance. With this, the Mughal troops became aware of the Singhs, And the location of the Singhs' houses and hamlets. (10)
lines: The Singhs then challenged the Mughals with the beat of a drum,
Which the Mughal troops heard from a distance.
With this, the Mughal troops became aware of the Singhs,
And the location of the Singhs' houses and hamlets.

blocks.text: A (friendly) Pathan, too, came running on a horseback, Warning the Singhs not to lose their lives in vain. As he had intimated them about the approaching troops, They should escape and take refuge in the wilds. (11)
lines: A (friendly) Pathan, too, came running on a horseback,
Warning the Singhs not to lose their lives in vain.
As he had intimated them about the approaching troops,
They should escape and take refuge in the wilds.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Tara Singh (acknowledging his service), told him, That he (Tara Singh) was indeed grateful to the brotherly Pathan. But since he had taken a vow to make a sacrifice, He would certainly sacrifice his life at his own place. (12)
lines: Tara Singh (acknowledging his service), told him,
That he (Tara Singh) was indeed grateful to the brotherly Pathan.
But since he had taken a vow to make a sacrifice,
He would certainly sacrifice his life at his own place.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

At that time S. Tara Singh was serving the other Singhs, By filling a big tub with water for bathing the Singhs. Then these Singhs beseeched Tara Singh while serving them, That he had already done a plenty of service to them. (13)
lines: At that time S.
Tara Singh was serving the other Singhs,
By filling a big tub with water for bathing the Singhs.
Then these Singhs beseeched Tara Singh while serving them,
That he had already done a plenty of service to them.

blocks.text: Now it was their turn to do some service to him, So that they could also sanctify their bodies with his service. At this, S. Tara Singh addressed his companions, That one's body was sanctified only after being wounded in a war. (14)
lines: Now it was their turn to do some service to him,
So that they could also sanctify their bodies with his service.
At this,
S.
Tara Singh addressed his companions,
That one's body was sanctified only after being wounded in a war.

blocks.text: Dohra:
As the devout get their bodies sanctified, By getting themselves branded at Dwarka2 . Similarly, when a warrior gets wounded in war. His body gets sanctified with the touch of a weapon. (15)
lines: As the devout get their bodies sanctified,
By getting themselves branded at Dwarka2 .
Similarly, when a warrior gets wounded in war.
His body gets sanctified with the touch of a weapon.

blocks.text: Chaupai:
As S. Tara Singh went out to fetch water, He spotted the Mughal troops advancing towards them. Returning, he announced to the Singhs once again, That anyone willing to escape should escape now. (16)
lines: As S.
Tara Singh went out to fetch water,
He spotted the Mughal troops advancing towards them.
Returning, he announced to the Singhs once again,
That anyone willing to escape should escape now.

blocks.text: Otherwise, they should come out with their weapons, And stand in the battlefield leaving their shelters. Hearing this, the Singhs came out in the open, Leaving their shelter, they stood on the battlefield. (17)
lines: Otherwise, they should come out with their weapons,
And stand in the battlefield leaving their shelters.
Hearing this, the Singhs came out in the open,
Leaving their shelter, they stood on the battlefield.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The Mughal troops launched an attack from the other side, With the beat of war drums and other trumpets. Launching their attack from all the four sides, They scattered like players in the rustic game of Sonchi3 . (18)
lines: The Mughal troops launched an attack from the other side,
With the beat of war drums and other trumpets.
Launching their attack from all the four sides,
They scattered like players in the rustic game of Sonchi3 .

blocks.text: Chaupai:

S. Bulakha Singh was the first to attack the invaders, Who wounded many Mughal soldiers with his sword. Then after being hit by an enemy arrow in the chest, He fell down and departed for his heavenly abode. (19)
lines: S.
Bulakha Singh was the first to attack the invaders,
Who wounded many Mughal soldiers with his sword.
Then after being hit by an enemy arrow in the chest,
He fell down and departed for his heavenly abode.

blocks.text: Then the Singhs stood in a circle with their backs towards each other, As if they were going to participate in the game of Sonchi. As the Mughal troops attacked these circled Singhs, They kept on repulsing their attack from their side. (20)
lines: Then the Singhs stood in a circle with their backs towards each other,
As if they were going to participate in the game of Sonchi.
As the Mughal troops attacked these circled Singhs,
They kept on repulsing their attack from their side.

blocks.text: So much dust and din was raised from both the sides, As if a dust storm had broke in at night. The Mughal soldiers while riding on their horses, Intended to crush the Singhs with horse's hooves. (21)
lines: So much dust and din was raised from both the sides,
As if a dust storm had broke in at night.
The Mughal soldiers while riding on their horses,
Intended to crush the Singhs with horse's hooves.

blocks.text: But as the Singh chopped off the horses heads, Their riders fell down feeling exhausted and defeated. Some of the horse mounted soldiers collided against each other, And fell down, blocking the passage of their own troops. (22)
lines: But as the Singh chopped off the horses heads,
Their riders fell down feeling exhausted and defeated.
Some of the horse mounted soldiers collided against each other,
And fell down, blocking the passage of their own troops.

blocks.text: Dohra:

As the soldiers from both the sides collided against each other, The passage got blocked with the falling bodies. As more and more soldiers came attacking, They too kept on falling on the heaped bodies. (23)
lines: As the soldiers from both the sides collided against each other,
The passage got blocked with the falling bodies.
As more and more soldiers came attacking,
They too kept on falling on the heaped bodies.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

While a few Mughal soldiers got wounded with their own weapons, Some others were hit by the weapons of advancing Singhs. There occurred such a blood bath from both sides, That soldiers from both sides got completely exhausted. (24)
lines: While a few Mughal soldiers got wounded with their own weapons,
Some others were hit by the weapons of advancing Singhs.
There occurred such a blood bath from both sides,
That soldiers from both sides got completely exhausted.

blocks.text: Thus, the attacks from both the sides slowed down, As it became difficult to wield small weapons in a close encounter. So the Mughal troops fired and shot arrows from a distance, And started killing Singhs while standing at a distance. (25)
lines: Thus, the attacks from both the sides slowed down,
As it became difficult to wield small weapons in a close encounter.
So the Mughal troops fired and shot arrows from a distance,
And started killing Singhs while standing at a distance.

blocks.text: Although the Singh had not any muskets or small fire arms, Yet the Mughals' bullets hit their own soldiers on the other side. Thereafter, Moman Khan himself, marching forward, Once again got an attack launched on the Singhs. (26)
lines: Although the Singh had not any muskets or small fire arms,
Yet the Mughals' bullets hit their own soldiers on the other side.
Thereafter,
Moman Khan himself, marching forward,
Once again got an attack launched on the Singhs.

blocks.text: At that Takki Khan4 , while advancing on his horse's back, Kept asking for S. Tara Singh's whereabouts (loudly). Hearing this, S. Tara Singh asked him to proceed a little further, And gave him option of attacking him (Tara Singh) first. (27)
lines: At that Takki Khan4 , while advancing on his horse's back,
Kept asking for S.
Tara Singh's whereabouts (loudly).
Hearing this,
S.
Tara Singh asked him to proceed a little further,
And gave him option of attacking him (Tara Singh) first.

blocks.text: As Takki Khan shot an arrow while riding on a horse, The arrow hit Tara Singh's headgear wrapped round his head. Leaping up, Tara Singh caught hold of Takki Khan's horse's reigns, Even as Takki Khan's entire body was protected with a steely armour. (28)
lines: As Takki Khan shot an arrow while riding on a horse,
The arrow hit Tara Singh's headgear wrapped round his head.
Leaping up,
Tara Singh caught hold of Takki Khan's horse's reigns,
Even as Takki Khan's entire body was protected with a steely armour.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Since the Mughal warrior was completely covered with a steel armour, No part of his entire body was (exposed) and visible. Tara Singh, spotting out Takki Khan's uncovered face, Pierced the tip of his (sharp) sword into his face. (29)
lines: Since the Mughal warrior was completely covered with a steel armour,
No part of his entire body was (exposed) and visible.
Tara Singh, spotting out Takki Khan's uncovered face,
Pierced the tip of his (sharp) sword into his face.

blocks.text: As Takki Khan turned back with a bleeding face, Moman Khan recognized him (from his facial features). Beckoning bleeding Taki Khan to come nearer to him, He asked him from where did he chew beetelnut leaves. (30)
lines: As Takki Khan turned back with a bleeding face,
Moman Khan recognized him (from his facial features).
Beckoning bleeding Taki Khan to come nearer to him,
He asked him from where did he chew beetelnut leaves.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

At this, Takki Khan told Moman Khan tauntingly, That Tara Singh was sitting there with the beetelnut packets. He could also have a taste of those if he dared, Instead of passing such taunting remarks from a distance. (31)
lines: At this,
Takki Khan told Moman Khan tauntingly,
That Tara Singh was sitting there with the beetelnut packets.
He could also have a taste of those if he dared,
Instead of passing such taunting remarks from a distance.

blocks.text: Hearing this, one of Moman Khan's subordinates standing there, Marched ahead and launched an attack on the Singhs. Asking the elephant driver to move his elephant, This warrior shot pairs of arrows in each and every attempt. (32)
lines: Hearing this, one of Moman Khan's subordinates standing there,
Marched ahead and launched an attack on the Singhs.
Asking the elephant driver to move his elephant,
This warrior shot pairs of arrows in each and every attempt.

blocks.text: Reckoning the Singhs to be wounded and exhausted, He asked the elephant driver to move his elephant further. Thinking that he being perched higher on an elephant's back, He would get the Singhs crushed under elephant's feet. (33)
lines: Reckoning the Singhs to be wounded and exhausted,
He asked the elephant driver to move his elephant further.
Thinking that he being perched higher on an elephant's back,
He would get the Singhs crushed under elephant's feet.

blocks.text: Feeling emboldened at the sight of Singhs being in a minority. He assessed their strength by taking a round on the elephant's back. Being known as a great warrior among the Mughal troops, He shot pairs of arrows in each attempt at the Singhs. (34)
lines: Feeling emboldened at the sight of Singhs being in a minority.
He assessed their strength by taking a round on the elephant's back.
Being known as a great warrior among the Mughal troops,
He shot pairs of arrows in each attempt at the Singhs.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Then Bhima Singh (from Peshawar) in a mood of Chivalrous ecstasy, Pounced upon his enemy like a ferocious lion. Catching the elephant by the ear and pressing it hard, He made the elephant to sit down in an instant. (35)
lines: Then Bhima Singh (from Peshawar) in a mood of Chivalrous ecstasy,
Pounced upon his enemy like a ferocious lion.
Catching the elephant by the ear and pressing it hard,
He made the elephant to sit down in an instant.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

But as Bhima Singh made a dash at the elephant's driver, His sword broke apart as it struck against the elephant's prod. While he killed the elephant's driver with a half-broken sword, He himself fainted from the blow of an elephant's prod. (36)
lines: But as Bhima Singh made a dash at the elephant's driver,
His sword broke apart as it struck against the elephant's prod.
While he killed the elephant's driver with a half-broken sword,
He himself fainted from the blow of an elephant's prod.

blocks.text: Noticing Bhima Ssingh fainting, Tara Singh rushed to his aid, While addressing Lakhmir Singh in following words: When both of them (Tara Singh and Lakhmir Singh) used to graze buffaloes, Lakhmir Singh used to jump over a couple of buffaloes. (37)
lines: Noticing Bhima Ssingh fainting,
Tara Singh rushed to his aid,
While addressing Lakhmir Singh in following words: When both of them (Tara Singh and Lakhmir Singh) used to graze buffaloes,
Lakhmir Singh used to jump over a couple of buffaloes.

blocks.text: Now since this Mughal's calf (elephant) was not so big, He should jump and kill the Mughal warrior atop the elephant. Answering Tara Singh in the same vein, Lakhmir Singh said, That he himself was thinking on the same limes. (38)
lines: Now since this Mughal's calf (elephant) was not so big,
He should jump and kill the Mughal warrior atop the elephant.
Answering Tara Singh in the same vein,
Lakhmir Singh said,
That he himself was thinking on the same limes.

blocks.text: In case Tara Singh permitted him to make an attempt, He would definitely be able to kill the Mughal warrior. Uttering these words, Lakhmir Singh pounced upon his enemy, As a sea falcon pounces upon the sea gulls. (39)
lines: In case Tara Singh permitted him to make an attempt,
He would definitely be able to kill the Mughal warrior.
Uttering these words,
Lakhmir Singh pounced upon his enemy,
As a sea falcon pounces upon the sea gulls.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Catching hold of a spear, the Singh made a dash, While challenging Moman Khan's subordinate loudly. The Mughal warrior also attacked from the other side, While shouting for his kill with a greater force. (40)
lines: Catching hold of a spear, the Singh made a dash,
While challenging Moman Khan's subordinate loudly.
The Mughal warrior also attacked from the other side,
While shouting for his kill with a greater force.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Then, Lakhmir Singh, rushing upon him overpowered him, And pierced Moman Khan's subordinate in the shoulder. As Lakhmir Singh's spear cut through his shoulder, He could neither wield his sword nor shoot his arrows. (41)
lines: Then,
Lakhmir Singh, rushing upon him overpowered him,
And pierced Moman Khan's subordinate in the shoulder.
As Lakhmir Singh's spear cut through his shoulder,
He could neither wield his sword nor shoot his arrows.

blocks.text: As one or two more Singhs reached to help Lakhmir Singh, They chased away the other Mughals from around the elephant, Lakhmir Singh, taking an advantage of this opportunity, Mounted the elephant by catching hold of a rope. (42)
lines: As one or two more Singhs reached to help Lakhmir Singh,
They chased away the other Mughals from around the elephant,
Lakhmir Singh, taking an advantage of this opportunity,
Mounted the elephant by catching hold of a rope.

blocks.text: Despatching Moman Khan's subordinate with one stroke of his sword, Lakhmir Singh drove the elephant away towards Singhs. Remarking that a single elephant being of no use., The Singhs would allot such elephants to each one of their servants. (43)
lines: Despatching Moman Khan's subordinate with one stroke of his sword,
Lakhmir Singh drove the elephant away towards Singhs.
Remarking that a single elephant being of no use.,
The Singhs would allot such elephants to each one of their servants.

blocks.text: Noticing the elephant returning without its rider, The Mughal troops fled away feeling defeated. At this, Moman Khan summoned the (muscular) Purbia5 soldiers, Who had been conferred with great wartime decorations. (44)
lines: Noticing the elephant returning without its rider,
The Mughal troops fled away feeling defeated.
At this,
Moman Khan summoned the (muscular) Purbia5 soldiers,
Who had been conferred with great wartime decorations.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Mansa Ram and Daya Ram were two of these warriors, As these were the names given to them respectively. They had been ordered to accompany the Mughal troops, And they hailed from the village named Kundalpur. (45)
lines: Mansa Ram and Daya Ram were two of these warriors,
As these were the names given to them respectively.
They had been ordered to accompany the Mughal troops,
And they hailed from the village named Kundalpur.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Making a dash, as they pounced upon the Singhs, The Singh also came into combat from the other side. Mansa Ram and Daya Ram, (the renowned Purbia warriors), Were (also) slaughtered by the Singhs at the same place. (46)
lines: Making a dash, as they pounced upon the Singhs,
The Singh also came into combat from the other side.
Mansa Ram and Daya Ram,
(the renowned Purbia warriors),
Were (also) slaughtered by the Singhs at the same place.

blocks.text: As the Mughal troops took to their heels, The Singhs came to dominate over this field of battle. But as visibility increased with the break of dawn, The Mughals made a fresh attempt to wrest the field. (47)
lines: As the Mughal troops took to their heels,
The Singhs came to dominate over this field of battle.
But as visibility increased with the break of dawn,
The Mughals made a fresh attempt to wrest the field.

blocks.text: While some Singhs were found standing here and there, Others were lying dead or prostrated with wounds. Since they were too scared to come near the Singhs, They fired shots with their muskets from a distance. (48)
lines: While some Singhs were found standing here and there,
Others were lying dead or prostrated with wounds.
Since they were too scared to come near the Singhs,
They fired shots with their muskets from a distance.

blocks.text: In this way, they killed all the remaining Singhs who survived, And then severed their heads from their bodies. In this way, S. Tara Singh sacrificed to attain martyrdom, Along with his twenty two companions who stood with him. (49)
lines: In this way, they killed all the remaining Singhs who survived,
And then severed their heads from their bodies.
In this way,
S.
Tara Singh sacrificed to attain martyrdom,
Along with his twenty two companions who stood with him.

blocks.text: Thus, S. Tara Singh accomplishing a legendary deed, Became famous (as a martyr) in the whole world. Following the great Guru's words in letter and spirit, He sacrificed his life rather than compromising his dignity. (50)
lines: Thus,
S.
Tara Singh accomplishing a legendary deed,
Became famous (as a martyr) in the whole world.
Following the great Guru's words in letter and spirit,
He sacrificed his life rather than compromising his dignity.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Praise be to those devout Singhs (of the Khalsa Panth), Who accomplished such a legendary deed, sacrificing their lives. Till eternity, will their great deeds survive and last, In this otherwise fleeting world of change and flux. (51)
lines: Praise be to those devout Singhs (of the Khalsa Panth),
Who accomplished such a legendary deed, sacrificing their lives.
Till eternity, will their great deeds survive and last,
In this otherwise fleeting world of change and flux.
